title: Control the Inputs Not the Outcomes
coreMove: Define success for a block by the input you can deliver, then release the outcome you cannot command.
sourcePressure: The chapter clarifies what the reader owns inside scheduled time: controllable effort and process signals, not guaranteed outcomes.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: A weak run would pretend outcomes do not matter instead of separating them from the controllable process.

hook: Control the Inputs Not the Outcomes as a labeled topic opener
counterintuition: phones are not the problem by itself
tryThisNow: set a timer and notice your distractions
examples: reused old-package object-anchor shell from earlier Indistractable run

exampleSpecs.domain: grant writer submitting a rural broadband proposal
exampleSpecs.stakes: waiting on approval can wreck the drafting block
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she defines the input as three clean budget justifications and stops refreshing the grant portal

exampleSpecs.domain: youth fencing coach preparing athletes for qualifiers
exampleSpecs.audience: coach who feels responsible for medals
exampleSpecs.stakes: training quality drops when results own the session
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he posts footwork reps as the input and leaves ranking boards covered
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A foil mask hangs beside a footwork ladder.

exampleSpecs.stakes: data collection suffers if the harvest outcome becomes the only measure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she checks irrigation logs and sample timing as the input before looking at yield estimates
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A soil core sleeve lies beside an irrigation log.

exampleSpecs.domain: bookstore events manager planning a poetry night
exampleSpecs.stakes: the event gets overmanaged if turnout controls the day
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before, he refreshes reservations; after, he defines success as calls to three local hosts and a clean chair layout
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A handbill proof sits near a seating sketch.

exampleSpecs.domain: appellate law student practicing oral argument
exampleSpecs.audience: student who wants praise from judges
exampleSpecs.stakes: practice becomes avoidance when applause is the measure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she counts the input as answering five hostile questions without notes
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A moot-court bench diagram sits beside five question cards.

exampleSpecs.audience: lookout who cannot control whether crews find the source
exampleSpecs.stakes: reporting precision matters more than certainty
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he writes wind direction, color, and bearing before asking whether he overreacted
